@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+# DeepSeek V4 DEP performance review
+
+This bundle records the frozen MI355X stack selected for human review on
+2026-10-26. Runtime code matches the measured `9db2dd585bd9` source diff against `df6603f0583375f244d1ac6d36265462b7490392`.
+`source_manifest.json` records the original per-file hashes and the review-only
+adaptations. The added report and
+configuration documentation do not change runtime behavior. Five synchronization
+calls in a graph test use the required `torch.accelerator` API; test assertions
+and tolerances are unchanged.
+
+## Scope and provenance
+
+This is an integration draft in Fangzhou-Ai/vllm. Existing upstream proposals
+retain ownership of their changes; this draft is not a replacement upstream PR.
+
+| Work | Provenance / local adaptation |
+| --- | --- |
+| Dense paged MXFP4 indexer | [#60834](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60834), applied commit `022b43c66f6c2b39c8f0e7c4813544481aca43c0`; real operator tests and 64-head coverage added locally |
+| DP prefill delayer | [#61834](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61834), head `27661316f53f26eb36b0980c8b5325bbc64141a0`; retained local cadence initialization and real Scheduler/AsyncScheduler tests |
+| ASM sparse MLA / native KV layout | [#61826](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61826), head `d36f02e274ae5cc395e37cf6d5e45cacf8152dce`; local planner accounting, minimum split correction, fast compressed decode and short-row correction |
+| WO_A FP8 BMM | One-time weight preshuffle and the matching AITER BMM, plus shared BF16 RoPE tables |
+| Router | Reuse the existing top-6 Triton router on gfx950 for supported shapes; stable softplus, deterministic ties, real padding mask, zero-row return |
+| E8M0 linears | Opt-in native scaled shared-expert, attention and draft GEMMs; exact checkpoint scale conversion; fused query RMSNorm/quantization |
+| Indexer TopK | Select native AITER TopK for gfx950, K=1024 and width=262144, including FULL graph replay |
+
+The DP-global gate from #62901, experimental Rust routing policies, the
+128-capacity MegaMoE trial, the newer prefill tile/configuration trials, dual
+scale cache prototypes and incomplete CPU offload work are excluded.
+
+## Measured balanced decode
+
+DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 FP4, 8x MI355X, Rust frontend, TP1/DP8/EP8,
+AITER MegaMoE + MoRI, K6 DSpark, synthetic acceptance length 3.77, no offload,
+uniform requests per rank, approximately 177K context, two ordered measurements
+per framework. The input fingerprint is identical across the listed stages.
+The earlier attention checkpoint already includes the fast sparse-attention path;
+these numbers do not represent a comparison against unmodified main.
+
+| Stage | c64 cycle ms | c96 cycle ms | c128 cycle ms |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Earlier fast-attention checkpoint | 41.708 | 47.050 | 51.615 |
+| Enable FP8 WO_A BMM / preshuffle | 39.821 | 45.109 | 49.301 |
+| Router + shared RoPE stack | 39.992 | 45.594 | 49.106 |
+| Native E8M0 shared MLP / WO_B | 39.353 | 45.199 | 48.486 |
+| Fused query norm + attention/draft E8M0 | 38.196 | 44.353 | 47.547 |
+| Selected stack + native indexer TopK | **37.497** | **43.838** | **46.684** |
+| Same-host ATOM control | 36.790 | 42.549 | 45.595 |
+| Selected latency above ATOM | 1.923% | 3.028% | 2.390% |
+
+Across the measured stages, cycle time falls 10.10%, 6.83% and 9.55% from the
+earlier fast-attention checkpoint. WO_A accounts for 4.13-4.52%; E8M0 MLP/WO_B
+for 0.87-1.60%; fused query/draft changes for 1.87-2.94%; TopK for 1.16-1.83%,
+each relative to its immediate parent. These percentages must not be added.
+Router + shared RoPE has operator/memory benefits but no consistent full-cycle
+speedup: its measured changes range from a 1.08% regression to a 0.40% reduction.
+
+Each `*_anchored_comparison.json` includes both repetitions and their spread.
+For the selected stack the observed range is 0.47%, 0.03%, 0.22% of its median.
+These are complete decode cycles including draft, CPU and communication, rather
+than isolated GPU target-forward timings. Uniform request counts remove queue
+skew but do not force uniform expert loads. Ordered repetitions do not establish
+statistical equivalence or remove drift. The ATOM source is pinned to the image
+source; the same-host runtime and rebuilt Rust binary differ from the published
+nightly. No claim of published ATOM parity follows from this comparison.
+
+## Serving and quality
+
+The selected stack's completed c64 AgentX run used 3600 seconds, ten warmups,
+consistent-hash routing, prefix-cache reset and no offload. See
+`canonical_c64.json` and `canonical_server.json` for accounting and the exact
+recorded launch. There were 6786 successful timed requests, no request errors,
+and 15 normal duration-cutoff cancellations.
+
+| c64 metric | Selected stack | Published ATOM target | Relative gap |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Output tok/s/node | 1881.749 | 1984.042 | -5.16% |
+| Input tok/s/node | 243301.514 | 254282.443 | -4.32% |
+| Total tok/s/node | 245183.263 | 256266.485 | -4.33% |
+| P90 interactivity tok/s/user | 59.555 | 65.888 | -9.61% |
+
+The newer paired-query prefill tile reached 1910.556 output tok/s/node but reduced
+P90 to 55.058; it is excluded from this PR. Its throughput increase alone does
+not establish an overall serving improvement. No final c48/c96/c128 canonical
+serving result or genuine-offload c256/c384 result is established.
+
+Real-verification evaluations compare an earlier ASM baseline to the entire
+selected stack, not the final TopK dispatch alone. Both arms have 786 scored
+responses, unchanged budgets and seed, zero empty outputs and no evaluator
+errors. See `quality.json` and `indexer_topk_quality_review_before_canonical.json`.
+
+| Evaluation | Earlier ASM baseline | Selected stack |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| GPQA | 338/396 | 330/396 |
+| AIME | 28/30 | 30/30 |
+| NIAH (32K / 128K / 256K, three variants) | 360/360 | 360/360 |
+
+The GPQA difference is -2.02 percentage points, with paired-cluster 95% interval
+[-4.80, +0.51]. A meaningful regression remains possible. Sixteen of the 18 lost
+outcomes reached the candidate output limit; no filtering or altered budgets
+were used. This draft does not claim quality equivalence. NIAH coverage includes
+105 actual target query rows on all eight ranks, not just requested concurrency.
+
+## Validation and reproduction
+
+The exact selected source previously passed 11 CPU + 35 real FP8 layer + 71
+attention/indexer/compressor + 16 router cases (133 total, no skips).
+`validation/summary.json`, JUnit XML and logs contain the fresh runs on this PR
+checkout. Commands use the uv-managed environment; AITER and MI355X are required
+for GPU cases. The selected public test entry points and environment are recorded
+in `validation/summary.json` and `canonical_server.json`.
+
+For example, from this checkout:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
+VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_DSV4_FP8_MXSCALE=1 \
+VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_ASM_SPARSE_MLA=1 VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1 \
+.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
+  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_dsv4_mxfp4_indexer.py \
+  tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py::test_dsv4_fast_topk
+```
+
+Regression coverage includes changed-input graph replay, actual pooled cache
+writers, all valid logits/TopK sets, large byte offsets, short rows, empty batches,
+leading dimensions, incompatible-scale fallback and compile/FakeTensor paths.
+An additional 17 CPU scheduler/cache-planner cases passed on the draft checkout.
+The existing AMD Buildkite kernel steps select the added GPU regressions.
+Large-model AgentX and quality runs remain external to CI.
+
+The compound MLP oracle correction is documented separately in
+`e8m0_mlp_reference_contract_addendum.json`: independent per-GEMM tolerances were
+retained, and the whole quantized pipeline requires exact equality to the same
+FP8 operands/scales on the ordinary GEMM path. The initial MLP oracle diagnostic evidence remains in the experiment directory.
+`prior_regressions/` includes the original failing and fixed ASM split checks
+and the failing delayer scheduling regression.
+
+## Review status
+
+This is a human-review draft. AI assistance was used for implementation, tests,
+analysis and PR preparation. The human submitter still needs to review every
+changed line, run the relevant validations and defend the change before any
+upstream submission. Remaining issues include the GPQA uncertainty, incomplete
+canonical concurrency matrix, and upstreaming the integration as appropriately
+scoped changes rather than duplicating the adopted proposals.

+# DeepSeek V4 DEP on MI355X
+
+This review branch supports DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 on eight MI355X GPUs with
+TP1, DP8 attention, EP8, AITER MegaMoE, MoRI and the Rust frontend. The native
+sparse-attention and E8M0 optimizations are opt-in and disabled by default.
+
+Set these variables before starting the server:
+
+```bash
+export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1
+export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
+export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
+export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
+export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=1
+export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_ASM_SPARSE_MLA=1
+export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_DSV4_FP8_MXSCALE=1
+export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0
+export AITER_MEGA_FIXED_SLOT_MAX_MTPR=511
+export MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=16G
+```
+
+Use the following options with your DeepSeek V4 model path and other serving
+settings:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 \
+  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 8 \
+  --enable-expert-parallel --enable-ep-weight-filter \
+  --moe-backend aiter_mega_moe --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
+  --async-scheduling --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}' \
+  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 16 \
+  --long-prefill-token-threshold 16384 \
+  --prefill-schedule-interval 1 \
+  --dp-prefill-delayer --dp-prefill-delayer-protected-steps 10 \
+  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[7,14,21,28,35,42,49,56,63,70,77,84,91,98,105,112]}' \
+  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
+  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
+  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+  --enable-prefix-caching --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
+  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86
+```
+
+This is the real-verification serving form. The recorded performance runs used
+synthetic acceptance length 3.77; they do not measure real draft acceptance.
+The configuration was validated through c128 balanced decode and c64 AgentX.
+The per-rank request limit is 16. Higher concurrency and CPU KV offload require
+separate validation. This branch's ASM cache layout rejects KV connectors and
+CPU offload because its separate RoPE pool is not transferred.
+
+## Native sparse attention and E8M0
+
+`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_ASM_SPARSE_MLA=1` requires gfx950, DeepSeek V4, TP1,
+128 local heads and `fp8_ds_mla` caches (selected by `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`).
+Decode quantizes queries to FP8. The native cache stores BF16 RoPE in a separate
+pool, which the planner accounts for; this reduces cache capacity. Prefill uses
+the existing attention path over the same cached values.
+
+`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_DSV4_FP8_MXSCALE=1` enables native E8M0 activation scales
+for compatible shared-expert, attention and DSpark draft projections. Weight
+scales must be exactly representable and satisfy the kernel layout restrictions;
+otherwise the layer retains its configured path. Query RMSNorm/quantization is
+fused only when both query consumers support the result. Power-of-two activation
+quantization changes numerical behavior, so evaluate quality on your workload.
+
+The gfx950 MXFP4 indexer automatically selects AITER TopK for K=1024 and a
+262144-column logits plane, including short batches and captured graph replay.
+It does not add another environment variable.
+
+## DP prefill delayer
+
+`--dp-prefill-delayer` is disabled by default. When enabled, ranks exchange
+prefill/decode state once per step through one CPU all-reduce and make the same
+prefill release decision. `--dp-prefill-delayer-protected-steps` defaults to 10
+and protects that many decode steps after a prefill. Aligning prefills can
+increase time to first token.
+
+The delayer requires `--prefill-schedule-interval 1`; it replaces the ordinary
+cadence. Elastic EP and custom scheduler classes are unsupported. This branch
+adopts [upstream PR #61834](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61834).
+The long-prefill threshold retains its existing exception for a sole local
+request, so setting a cap does not prove mixed-step duration is bounded.
+
+## Measured limits
+
+Balanced full decode cycles remain 1.9-3.0% above the same-host ATOM control at
+c64/c96/c128. The selected c64 AgentX result is 1881.75 output tok/s/node and
+59.56 P90 tok/s/user; it does not meet the published ATOM target. The real-model
+quality comparison returned NIAH 360/360, AIME 30/30 and GPQA 330/396, compared
+with 360/360, 28/30 and 338/396 for the earlier ASM baseline. Quality equivalence
+is unproven. The review bundle under `benchmarks/kernels/dsv4_dep_review/` contains
+per-stage timings, complete accounting and source hashes.

+## DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA on AMD MI355X
+
+`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_ASM_SPARSE_MLA` enables AITER's native-layout ASM attention
+for DeepSeek V4 decode on MI355X (`gfx950`). It is disabled by default. To enable
+it, set the variable before starting your DeepSeek V4 server:
+
+```bash
+export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_ASM_SPARSE_MLA=1
+```
+
+This path requires tensor parallelism of one, 128 local attention heads, and
+FP8 MLA KV caches. Use `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8`; DeepSeek
+V4 resolves the cache dtype to `fp8_ds_mla`. For an eight-GPU deployment, combine
+this with `--data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel` in your serving
+configuration.
+
+Decode uses FP8 queries and a native KV layout with a separate BF16 RoPE pool.
+Prefill uses the default attention path with the same cached values. The cache
+planner accounts for the additional pool, so fewer tokens fit at a fixed GPU
+memory budget. Assess model quality on your workload when changing query
+precision.
+
+Larger compressed decode batches use single-pass CSA or persistent HCA kernels.
+Short rows receive an FP32 softmax/value correction. The persistent workspace is
+allocated before GPU memory profiling and reduces the memory available for KV
+caches.
+
+KV transfer connectors and CPU KV offload are unsupported while this variable
+is enabled. The sparse indexer's KV dtype remains a separate setting under
+`--attention-config`.
+
+## DeepSeek V4 FP8 block scales on AMD MI355X
+
+`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_DSV4_FP8_MXSCALE=1` enables native UE8M0 activation
+and weight scales for compatible attention and shared-expert projections,
+including the DSpark draft model and its input projection.
+It requires AITER on `gfx950`, tensor parallelism of one, and FP8 weights
+with group-128 block scales that can be represented exactly as UE8M0.
+BF16 activations are required. The ASM sparse attention path also uses a fused
+query RMSNorm and UE8M0 quantizer for the attention and indexer query projections.
+Both consumers must have compatible scales before this producer is enabled.
+Other layers retain their configured quantization path.
+
+The option is disabled by default. It quantizes activation scales to powers
+of two and selects AITER's native scaled GEMMs. Evaluate model quality when
+changing activation quantization. Checkpoint weight scales are preserved
+losslessly; unsupported weights retain their FP32 scale path.
+
+## DeepSeek V4 indexer on AMD MI355X
+
+The MXFP4 indexer uses AITER's 1024-key top-k on `gfx950` with a
+262144-column logits plane, including small decode batches. This is the
+layout for DeepSeek V4's 1M token context with compression by four.
+The dispatch uses the device and tensor shape and supports changing row lengths
+inside a captured graph.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""DeepSeek-V4's ROCm MXFP4 indexer K writer: the pooling kernel plus aiter's
+norm + RoPE + MXFP4 cache op, against the same op fed by torch's pooling.
+
+The dense K6 path selects top1024/2048 against dequantized Torch scores at64heads.
+"""
+
+import itertools
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+    pytest.skip("ROCm-only", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from vllm.platforms.rocm import get_cdna_version
+
+if get_cdna_version() != 4:
+    pytest.skip("CDNA4-only", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from tests.kernels.attention.test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer import (
+    _assert_topk,
+    _dequant,
+    _scores,
+)
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.forward_context import set_forward_context
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.amd.rocm import (
+    compress_pool,
+)
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.indexer import DeepSeekV32IndexerDecodeMetadata
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer import (
+    RocmMxfp4IndexerMetadata,
+    native_decode,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer import (
+    build_rocm_mxfp4_decode_schedule,
+    rocm_mxfp4_decode_schedule_words,
+    rocm_mxfp4_indexer_k_store,
+    rocm_mxfp4_indexer_q_quant,
+    rocm_mxfp4_sparse_attn_indexer,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import init_workspace_manager, reset_workspace_manager
+
+# DeepSeek-V4-Pro's indexer: 64 heads of 128, ratio 4 with overlap, 256-token
+# blocks, so 64-entry K pages.
+HEADS, HEAD_DIM, RATIO, PAGE = 64, 128, 4, 64
+WIDTH = HEAD_DIM // 2 + HEAD_DIM // 32
+STATE_BLOCK, MAX_POS = 16, 4096
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+
+
+class _Case:
+    """Requests with random compressor states and their boundary tokens'
+    slots in a paged K cache."""
+
+    def __init__(self, seq_lens, max_pos=MAX_POS):
+        self.state_width = 2 * HEAD_DIM  # coff * head_dim, kv then score
+        state_blocks = sum(cdiv(n, STATE_BLOCK) for n in seq_lens)
+        self.state_cache = torch.randn(
+            state_blocks, STATE_BLOCK, 2 * self.state_width, device=DEVICE
+        )
+        width = max(cdiv(n, STATE_BLOCK) for n in seq_lens)
+        self.block_table = torch.zeros(
+            len(seq_lens), width, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE
+        )
+        perm = torch.randperm(state_blocks)
+        used = 0
+        for req, n in enumerate(seq_lens):
+            self.block_table[req, : cdiv(n, STATE_BLOCK)] = perm[
+                used : used + cdiv(n, STATE_BLOCK)
+            ]
+            used += cdiv(n, STATE_BLOCK)
+
+        self.positions = torch.cat([torch.arange(n) for n in seq_lens]).to(DEVICE)
+        self.req = torch.cat(
+            [torch.full((n,), r, dtype=torch.int32) for r, n in enumerate(seq_lens)]
+        ).to(DEVICE)
+        # each request's pages, scattered over a pool with spare pages
+        pages = [cdiv(cdiv(n, RATIO), PAGE) for n in seq_lens]
+        first_page = torch.tensor([0, *itertools.accumulate(pages)][:-1])
+        self.num_pages = sum(pages) + 2
+        page_of = torch.randperm(self.num_pages).to(DEVICE)
+        comp = self.positions // RATIO
+        page = page_of[first_page.to(DEVICE)[self.req.long()] + comp // PAGE]
+        boundary = (self.positions + 1) % RATIO == 0
+        self.kv_slot = torch.where(boundary, page * PAGE + comp % PAGE, -1)
+        self.cos_sin = torch.randn(max_pos, 64, device=DEVICE)
+        self.norm = torch.rand(HEAD_DIM, device=DEVICE) + 0.5
+
+    def torch_pooled(self):
+        """Softmax-gated pooling of each token's 2 * RATIO-token window: the
+        older RATIO tokens read the first state half, the newer the second."""
+        out = torch.zeros(len(self.positions), HEAD_DIM, device=DEVICE)
+        for t in range(len(self.positions)):
+            p = int(self.positions[t])
+            if (p + 1) % RATIO:
+                continue
+            kv, score = [], []
+            for j, q in enumerate(range(p - 2 * RATIO + 1, p + 1)):
+                if q < 0:
+                    continue
+                row = self.state_cache[
+                    self.block_table[self.req[t], q // STATE_BLOCK], q % STATE_BLOCK
+                ]
+                half = HEAD_DIM if j >= RATIO else 0
+                kv.append(row[half : half + HEAD_DIM])
+                half += self.state_width
+                score.append(row[half : half + HEAD_DIM])
+            out[t] = (torch.stack(kv) * torch.stack(score).softmax(0)).sum(0)
+        return out
+
+    def run_compressor(self):
+        """Run the real pooling and cache-write operators on the paged input."""
+        kv_cache = torch.zeros(
+            self.num_pages, PAGE, WIDTH, dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEVICE
+        )
+        pooled = torch.empty(
+            len(self.positions), HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE
+        )
+        compress_pool(
+            self.state_cache,
+            self.req,
+            self.positions,
+            self.kv_slot,
+            self.block_table,
+            STATE_BLOCK,
+            pooled,
+            self.state_width,
+            RATIO,
+            True,
+        )
+        rocm_mxfp4_indexer_k_store(
+            pooled,
+            self.positions,
+            self.cos_sin,
+            self.norm,
+            1e-6,
+            kv_cache,
+            self.kv_slot,
+            RATIO,
+            True,
+            num_heads=HEADS,
+        )
+        return pooled, kv_cache
+
+
+SEQ_LENS = pytest.mark.parametrize("seq_lens", [[37, 300, 5], [1, 260]])
+
+
+@SEQ_LENS
+def test_pooled_rows_match_torch(seq_lens):
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    case = _Case(seq_lens)
+    pooled, _ = case.run_compressor()
+    boundary = case.kv_slot >= 0
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        pooled[boundary].float(),
+        case.torch_pooled()[boundary],
+        atol=1e-2,
+        rtol=1e-2,
+    )
+
+
+@SEQ_LENS
+def test_k_pages_match_aiter_fed_by_torch(seq_lens):
+    """The pages hold what aiter writes from torch's pooling: the same layout,
+    and the same MXFP4 codes up to bf16 rounding of the pooled rows."""
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    case = _Case(seq_lens)
+    _, kv_cache = case.run_compressor()
+    ref = torch.zeros_like(kv_cache)
+    rocm_mxfp4_indexer_k_store(
+        case.torch_pooled().bfloat16(),
+        case.positions,
+        case.cos_sin,
+        case.norm,
+        1e-6,
+        ref,
+        case.kv_slot,
+        RATIO,
+        True,
+        num_heads=HEADS,
+    )
+    assert bool(ref.any())
+    assert (kv_cache != ref).float().mean().item() < 5e-3
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_requests", [6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("context", [10800, 170000])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("topk,logits_width", [(2048, None), (1024, 262144)])
+def test_k6_dense_selection_matches_torch_at_64_heads(
+    num_requests, context, topk, logits_width
+):
+    """DSV4's K6 path selects the quantized reference at its native logits stride.
+
+    Real pooling, writers, Q quantization, metadata and forward context feed
+    the public indexer op. The reference reads token-major keys, independent
+    of the shuffled, strided pages consumed by the indexer.
+    """
+    from aiter.ops.triton.fusions.k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache import (
+        k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache,
+    )
+
+    set_random_seed(42)
+    next_n = 7
+    seq_lens = [context + 23 * r for r in range(num_requests)]
+    case = _Case(seq_lens, max_pos=max(seq_lens))
+    pooled, contiguous_cache = case.run_compressor()
+    pool = torch.zeros(
+        case.num_pages, PAGE * WIDTH + 576, dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEVICE
+    )
+    cache = torch.as_strided(pool, contiguous_cache.shape, (pool.stride(0), WIDTH, 1))
+    cache.copy_(contiguous_cache)
+    offsets = [0, *itertools.accumulate(n // RATIO for n in seq_lens)]
+    prefix = torch.tensor(offsets[:-1], device=DEVICE)
+    natural = torch.zeros(offsets[-1], 1, WIDTH, dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEVICE)
+    boundary = case.kv_slot >= 0
+    natural_slots = torch.where(
+        boundary, prefix[case.req.long()] + case.positions // RATIO, -1
+    )
+    k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache(
+        pooled,
+        case.positions,
+        case.cos_sin,
+        case.norm,
+        1e-6,
+        natural,
+        natural_slots,
+        RATIO,
+    )
+    positions = torch.tensor(
+        [p for n in seq_lens for p in range(n - next_n, n)],
+        dtype=torch.int64,
+        device=DEVICE,
+    )
+    rows = len(positions)
+    (q, q_scale), weights = rocm_mxfp4_indexer_q_quant(
+        positions,
+        torch.randn(rows, HEADS, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE),
+        case.cos_sin,
+        torch.rand(rows, HEADS, device=DEVICE),
+        HEAD_DIM**-0.5,
+        HEADS**-0.5,
+    )
+    q_ref = _dequant(q, q_scale.view(torch.uint8).reshape(rows, HEADS, -1))
+    row_lens = ((positions + 1) // RATIO).to(torch.int32)
+    context_lens = torch.tensor(
+        [n // RATIO for n in seq_lens], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE
+    )
+    width = max(cdiv(n // RATIO, PAGE) for n in seq_lens)
+    block_table = torch.zeros(num_requests, width, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    for req in range(num_requests):
+        slots = case.kv_slot[(case.req == req) & boundary]
+        pages = (slots[::PAGE] // PAGE).to(torch.int32)
+        block_table[req, : len(pages)] = pages
+    row_table = block_table.repeat_interleave(next_n, dim=0)
+    query_lens = [next_n] * num_requests
+    native = native_decode(row_lens, row_table, query_lens, next_n, context_lens)
+    assert native is not None
+    max_context = max(seq_lens) // RATIO
+    logits_width = logits_width or max_context
+    schedule = torch.empty(
+        rocm_mxfp4_decode_schedule_words(HEADS, HEAD_DIM, PAGE, next_n),
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device=DEVICE,
+    )
+    metadata = RocmMxfp4IndexerMetadata(
+        seq_lens=torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE),
+        max_seq_len=max(seq_lens),
+        slot_mapping=torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.int64, device=DEVICE),
+        num_decodes=num_requests,
+        num_decode_tokens=rows,
+        num_prefills=0,
+        num_prefill_tokens=0,
+        decode=DeepSeekV32IndexerDecodeMetadata(
+            block_table=row_table,
+            seq_lens=row_lens.reshape(num_requests, next_n),
+            decode_lens=torch.full(
+                (num_requests,), next_n, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE
+            ),

+def _pack_asm_nope_reference(x):
+    nope = x[..., :448].float().reshape(*x.shape[:-1], 7, 64)
+    exponents = (nope.abs().amax(dim=-1) / 448).clamp_min(1e-4).log2().ceil()

+    packed[..., :448] = quantized.flatten(-2).view(torch.uint8)
+    packed[..., 448:462] = (exponents + 127).to(torch.uint8).repeat_interleave(2, -1)
+    dequantized = torch.cat(
+        ((quantized.float() * scales[..., None]).flatten(-2), x[..., 448:].float()), -1
+    )
+    return packed.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn), dequantized

+def _e8m0_mlp_reference(x, layer, gate_weight, gate_scale, down_weight, down_scale):
+    from aiter import gemm_a8w8_blockscale
+    from aiter.ops.quant import per_group_quant_hip
+
+    shape = x.shape
+    if x.numel() == 0:
+        return x.new_empty((*shape[:-1], down_weight.shape[0]))
+
+    def matmul(value, weight, scale):
+        m, k = value.shape
+        n = weight.shape[0]
+        quantized, encoded = per_group_quant_hip(
+            value,
+            quant_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn,
+            group_size=128,
+            transpose_scale=True,
+            scale_type=torch.float8_e8m0fnu,
+        )
+        decoded = torch.exp2(
+            encoded.view(torch.uint8).float().reshape(k // 128, m).T - 127
+        )
+        lhs = (
+            quantized.float().reshape(m, k // 128, 128) * decoded[..., None]
+        ).reshape(m, k)
+        rhs = (
+            weight.float().reshape(n // 128, 128, k // 128, 128)
+            * scale[:, None, :, None]
+        ).reshape(n, k)
+        reference = (lhs @ rhs.T).bfloat16()
+        baseline = gemm_a8w8_blockscale(
+            quantized, weight, decoded.contiguous(), scale, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            baseline.float(), reference.float(), atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2
+        )
+        # Requantization can amplify small GEMM rounding differences. Use the
+        # established FP8 arithmetic for the complete layer comparison.
+        return baseline
+
+    gate = matmul(x.reshape(-1, shape[-1]), gate_weight, gate_scale)
+    activated = layer.act_fn(gate)
+    result = matmul(activated, down_weight, down_scale)
+    return result.reshape(*shape[:-1], result.shape[-1])

+        assert delayer.decide(*full[:5], ran=int(i == 0)) == (False, "protected")

+"""DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA decode on aiter's v4 nm ASM kernels with FP8 Q
+(VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_ASM_SPARSE_MLA).
+
+Layout. Every DeepSeek-V4 attention cache page (SWA and compressed, target and
+DSpark draft) holds 512-byte rows, the packed row of aiter's v4 nm kernels:
+448 fp8 NoPE | 14 UE8M0 bytes (the 7 per-64 scales, each twice) | 50 pad.
+The bf16 RoPE (64 values) of a row lives in a side pool outside vLLM's KV
+allocation. Rows are named by r = (byte offset in the KV backing buffer) / 512,
+the same number in both pools: the kernels read row r at kv_base + 512 r and its
+RoPE at rope_base + 128 r. The backing buffer is block-outermost, so a layer's
+rows are not contiguous; r stays linear because every page offset and the block
+stride are multiples of 512 (asserted in register()). The side pool spans the
+whole buffer, 1/4 of its bytes, so the KV planner gives the cache 4/5 of the
+memory.
+
+A layer's cache view [NB, R, 512] (R rows a page) is Geom(c, k, R): the page of
+block b starts at row c + b k. Index lists are kept relative to a per-call base
+row, so the layer-independent part f(slot) = (slot // R) k + slot % R is computed
+once a step.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv, round_up
+
+ENABLED = envs.VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_ASM_SPARSE_MLA
+
+ROW_BYTES = 512
+NOPE_DIM = 448
+ROPE_DIM = 64
+HEADS = 128  # the v4 nm entry point used here (gqa 128, one query row a sequence)
+MAX_SPLITS = 16  # aiter never picks more for v4 nm
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Geom:
+    c: int  # row of block 0's page (512-byte rows from the buffer start)
+    k: int  # rows between consecutive blocks
+    R: int  # rows (states) a page
+    nb: int  # blocks
+
+
+class _State:
+    table_size: int = 0
+    storage_ptr: int = -1
+    raw: torch.Tensor | None = None  # uint8 [rows, 512], the whole KV buffer
+    raw_fp8: torch.Tensor | None = None  # same bytes as fp8
+    rope: torch.Tensor | None = None  # bf16 [rows, 64]
+    arange: torch.Tensor | None = None  # int32 [table_size + 1]
+    zeros: torch.Tensor | None = None  # int32 [table_size]
+    split_table: torch.Tensor | None = None  # int32 [MAX_SPLITS, table_size + 1]
+    rope_tables: dict[int, tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = {}
+    weights: dict[int, torch.Tensor] = {}
+    ps_workspace: Any = None
+
+
+_S = _State()
+
+
+def configure(vllm_config) -> None:
+    """Size the index tables: tokens a step, or the C128A top-k row width."""
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.sparse_mla import _C128A_TOPK_ALIGNMENT
+    from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        raise NotImplementedError("ASM sparse MLA requires gfx950.")
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx950
+
+    config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
+    if not on_gfx950() or config.model_type != "deepseek_v4":
+        raise NotImplementedError("ASM sparse MLA requires DeepSeek V4 on gfx950.")
+    if (
+        vllm_config.parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size != 1
+        or config.num_attention_heads != HEADS
+        or config.head_dim != 512
+        or config.qk_rope_head_dim != ROPE_DIM
+    ):
+        raise NotImplementedError(
+            "ASM sparse MLA requires 128 local heads of size 512."
+        )
+    if vllm_config.cache_config.cache_dtype != "fp8_ds_mla":
+        raise ValueError("ASM sparse MLA requires fp8_ds_mla KV caches.")
+    if (
+        vllm_config.kv_transfer_config is not None
+        or vllm_config.cache_config.kv_offloading_size is not None
+    ):

+    c128a_width = round_up(
+        cdiv(vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len, 128), _C128A_TOPK_ALIGNMENT

+    _S.table_size = max(
+        _S.table_size,
+        vllm_config.scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens,

+
+
+def _persistent_workspace(device):
+    if _S.ps_workspace is None:
+        assert not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing(), (
+            "Prepare persistent attention workspace before graph capture"
+        )
+        import aiter.mla as am
+
+        _S.ps_workspace = am.get_mla_v4_nm_ps_workspace(device, num_partitions=128)
+    return _S.ps_workspace
+
+
+def register(cache: torch.Tensor) -> Geom:
+    """Check a bound cache view [NB, R, 512] and return its geometry; the first
+    call for a backing buffer allocates the side pool and the decode tables
+    (KV binding runs before CUDA-graph capture)."""
+    assert ENABLED and _S.table_size > 0
+    assert cache.dtype == torch.uint8 and cache.dim() == 3, (cache.dtype, cache.shape)
+    nb, R, row = cache.shape
+    assert row == ROW_BYTES and cache.stride(2) == 1 and cache.stride(1) == ROW_BYTES, (
+        f"cache view must be [NB, R, 512] with 512-byte rows, got "
+        f"{tuple(cache.shape)} / {cache.stride()}"
+    )
+    storage = cache.untyped_storage()
+    base = storage.data_ptr()
+    off = cache.data_ptr() - base
+    assert off % ROW_BYTES == 0 and cache.stride(0) % ROW_BYTES == 0, (
+        f"page offset {off} / block stride {cache.stride(0)} not 512-aligned"
+    )
+    if _S.storage_ptr != base:
+        rows = storage.nbytes() // ROW_BYTES
+        dev = cache.device
+        _S.raw = cache.as_strided((rows, ROW_BYTES), (ROW_BYTES, 1), 0)
+        _S.raw_fp8 = _S.raw.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        _S.rope = None  # free a previous (profiling) pool first
+        _S.rope = torch.zeros((rows, ROPE_DIM), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
+        _S.storage_ptr = base
+        if _S.arange is None:
+            n = _S.table_size + 1
+            _S.arange = torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+            _S.zeros = torch.zeros(_S.table_size, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+            splits = torch.arange(1, MAX_SPLITS + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+            _S.split_table = splits[:, None] * _S.arange[None, :]
+    k = cache.stride(0) // ROW_BYTES
+    c = off // ROW_BYTES
+    assert c < k, (c, k)
+    return Geom(c=c, k=k, R=R, nb=nb)
+
+
+def rope_view(g: Geom) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The layer's RoPE rows as [NB, R, 64] bf16 (block stride k * 64)."""
+    assert _S.rope is not None
+    return _S.rope.as_strided(
+        (g.nb, g.R, ROPE_DIM), (g.k * ROPE_DIM, ROPE_DIM, 1), g.c * ROPE_DIM
+    )
+
+
+def _rows(slots: torch.Tensor, g: Geom) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """f(slot) = (slot // R) k + slot % R, -1 where slot < 0 (int32)."""
+    s = slots.to(torch.int32)
+    r = torch.where(
+        s >= 0,
+        torch.div(s, g.R, rounding_mode="floor") * g.k + torch.remainder(s, g.R),
+        -1,
+    )
+    return r.to(torch.int32)
+
+
+def _step() -> dict:
+    """Index lists shared by the layers of one step, kept on the forward
+    context so a new step never sees an old entry."""
+    from vllm.forward_context import get_forward_context
+
+    fc = get_forward_context()
+    st = getattr(fc, "_asm_sparse_mla_step", None)
+    if st is None:
+        st = {}
+        fc._asm_sparse_mla_step = st  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    return st
+
+
+def _prepare_tables(attn) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """bf16 cos / sin [max_pos, 32] and the bf16 kv_norm weight of a layer."""
+    cs = attn.rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache
+    t = _S.rope_tables.get(cs.data_ptr())
+    w = _S.weights.get(id(attn))
+    if t is None or w is None:
+        assert not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing(), (
+            "tables must be prepared before CUDA-graph capture"
+        )
+        if t is None:
+            half = cs.shape[-1] // 2
+            t = (
+                cs[:, :half].to(torch.bfloat16).contiguous(),
+                cs[:, half:].to(torch.bfloat16).contiguous(),
+            )
+            _S.rope_tables[cs.data_ptr()] = t
+        if w is None:
+            w = attn.kv_norm.weight.data.to(torch.bfloat16).contiguous()
+            _S.weights[id(attn)] = w
+    return t[0], t[1], w
+

+def qk_insert(
+    attn,
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_raw: torch.Tensor,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    slot_mapping: torch.Tensor,
+    num_decode_tokens: int,

+    """Q RMSNorm + RoPE (+ FP8 group quant for decode rows) and K RMSNorm + RoPE
+    + UE8M0 quant + SWA row write, on aiter's fused_qk_norm_rope_group_quant.

+    ``kv_raw`` is the pre-norm kv (the kernel applies kv_norm). Decode rows'
+    packed Q goes to ``attn._v4_q`` for the ASM decode; the returned bf16 q holds
+    the prefill rows (decode rows are left unset)."""

+        fused_qk_norm_rope_group_quant,
+    )

+    assert _S.raw_fp8 is not None and _S.rope is not None and _S.zeros is not None

+    T, H, D = q.shape
+    st = _step()
+    key = ("swa_rows", slot_mapping.data_ptr(), g.R, g.k, T)
+    dest = st.get(key)
+    if dest is None:
+        dest = _rows(slot_mapping[:T], g)
+        st[key] = dest
+    nope_rows = _S.raw_fp8[g.c :]
+    rope_rows = _S.rope[g.c :]

+    td = min(num_decode_tokens, T)
+    common: dict[str, Any] = dict(
+        k_weight=kw,
+        cos_cache=cos,
+        sin_cache=sin,
+        eps=attn.eps,
+        is_neox=False,
+        swa_nope_scale_buff=nope_rows,
+        swa_rope_buff=rope_rows,
+    )
+    if td > 0:
+        qp = torch.empty((td, H, D), dtype=dtypes.fp8, device=q.device)
+        qr = torch.empty((td, H, ROPE_DIM), dtype=q.dtype, device=q.device)
+        fused_qk_norm_rope_group_quant(
+            q[:td],
+            kv_raw[:td],
+            positions=positions[:td],
+            q_nope_scale_buff=qp,
+            q_rope_buff=qr,
+            swa_dest_row=dest[:td],
+            batch_id_per_token=bid[:td],
+            **common,
+        )

+        fused_qk_norm_rope_group_quant(
+            q[td:],
+            kv_raw[td:],
+            positions=positions[td:],
+            q_nope_scale_buff=q_out[td:],
+            swa_dest_row=dest[td:],
+            batch_id_per_token=bid[: T - td],
+            **common,
+        )
+    return q_out
+

+def _swa_dense(swa_md, gs: Geom, T: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Step-shared dense SWA rows f_s [T, W] (-1 beyond each row's length) and
+    its 0/1 validity."""
+    assert _S.arange is not None
+    st = _step()
+    key = ("swa_dense", id(swa_md))
+    hit = st.get(key)
+    if hit is None:
+        w = swa_md.decode_swa_width
+        dense = swa_md.decode_swa_indices.reshape(-1, w)[:T]
+        lens = swa_md.decode_swa_lens[:T]
+        col = _S.arange[:w]
+        valid = (col[None, :] < lens[:, None]) & (dense >= 0)
+        f = torch.where(valid, _rows(dense, gs), -1).to(torch.int32)
+        hit = (f, valid.to(torch.int32))
+        st[key] = hit
+    return hit
+
+
+def _row_lens(swa_md, T: int, width: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    st = _step()
+    key = ("row_lens", id(swa_md), T, width)
+    hit = st.get(key)
+    if hit is None:
+        valid = swa_md.is_valid_token[:T]
+        hit = torch.where(valid, width, 0).to(torch.int32)

+                st[key] = hit

+            block_table = attn_md.block_table[:num_decodes]
+            ComputeGlobalTopkIndicesAndLensKernel.kernel[(T,)](
+                dense[:, w:],
+                w + K,
+                lens,

+    RS0: tl.constexpr,

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Cross-DP prefill delayer.
+
+The DP ranks of a MoE model step in lockstep, so a step in which any rank runs
+prefill is a long step for every rank. Once per engine step all ranks
+all-reduce their prefill state and take the same decision: FIRE lets every rank
+with prefill work run it in the next step, HOLD defers all prefill (new requests
+and in-progress chunks) on every rank. The rules follow ATOM's PrefillDelayer.
+"""
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler import Scheduler
+
+# FIRE once the pending prefill tokens fill this fraction of the prefillable
+# ranks' token budgets.
+FILL_TARGET = 0.9
+# Upper bounds on HOLD, in steps.
+TTFT_MAX_HOLD_STEPS = 200
+PARTIAL_MAX_HOLD_STEPS = 100
+STALL_STEPS = 10
+# FIRE when a prefillable rank's KV cache usage reaches this fraction.
+KV_HIGH_USAGE = 0.9
+
+
+def local_state(scheduler: "Scheduler", token_budget: int) -> list[int]:
+    """[prefillable, pending prefill tokens (capped), decodes, KV high,
+    chunk in progress, prefill ran since the last call] of one rank."""
+    pending = decodes = partial = waiting = 0
+    for request in scheduler.running:
+        if request.is_prefill_chunk:
+            partial = 1
+            pending += max(request.num_tokens - request.num_computed_tokens, 0)
+        else:
+            decodes += 1
+    for request in scheduler.waiting:
+        if request in scheduler.deferred_waiting:
+            continue
+        waiting = 1
+        if pending >= token_budget:
+            break
+        pending += max(request.num_tokens - request.num_computed_tokens, 0)
+    prefillable = int(bool(partial or waiting))
+    kv_high = int(
+        bool(prefillable) and scheduler.kv_cache_manager.usage >= KV_HIGH_USAGE
+    )
+    ran = int(scheduler.ran_prefill)
+    scheduler.ran_prefill = False
+    return [prefillable, min(pending, token_budget), decodes, kv_high, partial, ran]
+
+
+class PrefillDelayer:
+    def __init__(self, dp_size: int, token_budget: int, protected_steps: int):
+        self.dp_size = dp_size
+        self.token_budget = token_budget
+        self.protected_steps = protected_steps
+        self._buf = torch.zeros(6, dtype=torch.int64)
+        self._first = True
+        self.reset()
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        self._protected_left = 0
+        self._hold_steps = 0
+        self._stall_steps = 0
+        self._prev_pending = -1
+
+    def step(self, scheduler: "Scheduler", dp_group: dist.ProcessGroup) -> bool:
+        """Returns whether the next step may run prefill. Must run on every DP
+        rank in every engine step (a CPU all-reduce on the DP group)."""
+        self._buf.copy_(
+            torch.tensor(local_state(scheduler, self.token_budget), dtype=torch.int64)
+        )
+        dist.all_reduce(self._buf, op=dist.ReduceOp.SUM, group=dp_group)
+        fire, _ = self.decide(*self._buf.tolist())
+        return fire
+
+    def decide(
+        self,
+        num_prefillable: int,
+        pending: int,
+        decodes: int,
+        kv_high: int,
+        partial: int,
+        ran: int,
+    ) -> tuple[bool, str]:
+        """FIRE (True) or HOLD (False) from the DP-summed state, with the rule
+        that decided it."""
+        if ran:
+            self._protected_left = self.protected_steps
+        if self._first:
+            self._first = False
+            return self._fire("first")
+        if self._protected_left > 0:
+            self._protected_left -= 1
+            if num_prefillable and decodes:
+                return False, "protected"
+        if num_prefillable == 0:
+            return self._fire("no_prefill")
+        if decodes == 0:
+            return self._fire("no_decode")
+        if kv_high:
+            return self._fire("kv_high")
+        if self._hold_steps >= TTFT_MAX_HOLD_STEPS:
+            return self._fire("ttft")
+        if partial and self._hold_steps >= PARTIAL_MAX_HOLD_STEPS:
+            return self._fire("partial")
+        if num_prefillable < self.dp_size:
+            return self._hold("align")
+        if pending >= FILL_TARGET * num_prefillable * self.token_budget:
+            return self._fire("fill")
+        if pending <= self._prev_pending:
+            self._stall_steps += 1
+        else:
+            self._stall_steps = 0
+        self._prev_pending = pending
+        if self._stall_steps >= STALL_STEPS:
+            return self._fire("stall")
+        return self._hold("fill")
+
+    def _fire(self, reason: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
+        self._hold_steps = 0
